subject: biochemistry
title: Lipoprotein metabolism: apolipoproteins, receptor pathways, and dyslipidemias

steps.tx: Lipoproteins transport insoluble triacylglycerols and cholesterol esters through the bloodstream encapsulated by an amphipathic monolayer of phospholipids, free cholesterol, and apolipoproteins. **Apolipoproteins** provide structural stability, serve as enzyme cofactors, and act as ligands for receptor-mediated clearance. Chylomicrons carry dietary lipids via Apo B-48. VLDL delivers endogenous hepatic triacylglycerols via Apo B-100. LDL transports cholesterol esters to peripheral tissues, and HDL mediates reverse cholesterol transport.
steps.say: Lipoproteins transport hydrophobic lipids encapsulated by phospholipids and apolipoproteins. Chylomicrons transport dietary fat via Apo B-48, VLDL carries hepatic triglycerides via Apo B-100, LDL delivers cholesterol, and HDL drives reverse cholesterol transport.

rows: Apo B-48, Apo C-II, Apo E
Apo B-100, Apo C-II, Apo E

steps.tx: Capillary endothelial **lipoprotein lipase** (LPL) hydrolyzes core triacylglycerols in chylomicrons and VLDL, releasing free fatty acids for muscular oxidation and adipose storage. LPL requires apolipoprotein C-II as an obligatory cofactor. Depleted chylomicrons become chylomicron remnants, cleared by hepatic LDL-receptor-related protein via apolipoprotein E. VLDL remnants (IDL) are either cleared by the liver or further hydrolyzed by hepatic lipase to yield **LDL**, which contains solely Apo B-100.
steps.say: Endothelial lipoprotein lipase hydrolyzes triglycerides in chylomicrons and VLDL, activated by Apo C-II. Remnants are cleared via Apo E. IDL undergoes hepatic lipase cleavage to generate LDL containing only Apo B-100.

nodes.label: Hepatic lipase converts IDL into LDL
Apo B-100 mediates peripheral LDL uptake

steps.tx: Reverse cholesterol transport is driven by **HDL** particles. Liver and intestine synthesize lipid-poor Apo A-I, which acquires free cholesterol from peripheral tissues via ABCA1 transporters. Lecithin-cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT), activated by Apo A-I, esterifies free cholesterol into hydrophobic cholesterol esters, driving them into the HDL core. Cholesterol ester transfer protein (CETP) exchanges HDL cholesterol esters for VLDL triacylglycerols, directing cholesterol toward hepatic clearance via scavenger receptor BI.
steps.say: Reverse cholesterol transport moves peripheral cholesterol to the liver via HDL. Apo A-I activates LCAT to trap cholesterol as core esters. CETP exchanges HDL cholesterol esters with VLDL triglycerides, while hepatic SR-BI mediates final clearance.

rows: Transfers HDL cholesterol esters to VLDL/LDL
Effluxes cellular cholesterol to nascent HDL

steps.tx: Familial **hypercholesterolemia** (Type IIa dyslipidemia) results from autosomal dominant loss-of-function mutations in the LDL receptor or Apo B-100, or gain-of-function mutations in PCSK9. Impaired LDL clearance causes profound hypercholesterolemia, tendon xanthomas (especially Achilles tendon), xanthelasma, and premature coronary artery atherosclerosis. Heterozygotes suffer myocardial infarction in their 30s to 40s, while homozygotes manifest fatal coronary disease before age 20 unless treated with PCSK9 inhibitors or LDL apheresis.
steps.say: Familial hypercholesterolemia stems from defective LDL receptors or Apo B-100, causing severe hypercholesterolemia, Achilles tendon xanthomas, and premature myocardial infarction. PCSK9 monoclonal antibodies prevent receptor destruction, lowering LDL.

nodes.label: Mutant LDL receptor or PCSK9 excess
Severe elevation of circulating plasma LDL
Endothelial lipid oxidation & foam cell formation
